2.w: “Listen carefully to my words; let this be the consolation you offer me.

3.w: Bear with me and I will speak, and after I have spoken you may mock.

4.w: Is my complaint against a man? If so, why should I not be impatient?

5.w: Look at me and be appalled; put your hands over your mouths.

6.w: For, when I think about this, I am terrified and my body feels a shudder.

7.w: “Why do the wicked go on living, grow old, even increase in power?

8.w: Their children are firmly established in their presence, their offspring before their eyes.

9.w: Their houses are safe and without fear; and no rod of punishment from God is upon them.

10.w: Their bulls breed without fail; their cows calve and do not miscarry.

11.w: They allow their children to run like a flock; their little ones dance about.

12.w: They sing to the accompaniment of tambourine and harp, and make merry to the sound of the flute.

13.w: They live out their years in prosperity and go down to the grave in peace.

14.w: So they say to God, ‘Turn away from us! We do not want to know your ways.

15.w: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What would we gain if we were to pray to him?’

16.w: But their prosperity is not their own doing. The counsel of the wicked is far from me!

17.w: “How often is the lamp of the wicked extinguished? How often does their misfortune come upon them? How often does God apportion pain to them in his anger?

18.w: How often are they like straw before the wind and like chaff swept away by a whirlwind?

19.w: You may say, ‘God stores up a man’s punishment for his children!’ Instead let him repay the man himself so that he may be humbled!

20.w: Let his own eyes see his destruction; let him drink of the anger of the Almighty.

21.w: For what is his interest in his home after his death, when the number of his months has been broken off?

22.w: Can anyone teach God knowledge, since he judges those that are on high?

23.w: “One man dies in his full vigor, completely secure and prosperous,

24.w: his body well nourished, and the marrow of his bones moist.

25.w: And another man dies in bitterness of soul, never having tasted anything good.

26.w: Together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover over them both.

27.w: “Yes, I know what you are thinking, the schemes by which you would wrong me.

28.w: For you say, ‘Where now is the nobleman’s house, and where are the tents in which the wicked lived?’

29.w: Have you never questioned those who travel the roads? Do you not recognize their accounts —

30.w: that the evil man is spared from the day of his misfortune, that he is delivered from the day of God’s wrath?

31.w: No one denounces his conduct to his face; no one repays him for what he has done.

32.w: And when he is carried to the tombs and watch is kept over the funeral mound,

33.w: the clods of the torrent valley are sweet to him; behind him everybody follows in procession, and before him goes a countless throng.

34.w: So how can you console me with your futile words? Nothing is left of your answers but deception!”
